answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a deposit that only grows along a spiral of verified honest work, so a fresh identity starts with nothing and cannot earn until it proves itself. Its opal-like attestation record, a signed tamper-evident trail of past deals, lets peers verify history cheaply, while sable-dark audit logs flag sudden clusters of identical new agents. One fake is cheap; hundreds with real history and locked deposits cost far more than any reward.
